newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Tribunal submits report on Bhutto brother's murder.
newsitem.headline: Tribunal submits report on Bhutto brother's murder.

text.p: A judicial tribunal submitted its report on Saturday on the killing of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza Bhutto.

The three-member tribunal was set up on October 18 under Justice Nasir Aslam Zahid, a Supreme Court judge, to investigate the death of Murtaza, killed with seven companions on September 20 near his home in the southern port city of Karachi.

Police have accused Bhutto's husband Asif Ali Zardari, former chief minister of Sindh province Abdullah Shah, former Intelligence Bureau chief Masood Sharif and 19 police officers, including Karachi's former deputy inspector general of police Shoaib Suddle, of involvement in the murder.
Advocate General Raja Qureshi, who received the report, said it would be presented to Sindh Chief Minister Liaquat Jatoi and the government would decide whether it should be made public.
Zahid told reporters the tribunal had recommended that its report be published.

In her testimony to the tribunal, Bhutto said her brother's murder was part of a plot to overthrow her government, which was sacked by President Farooq Leghari on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Zardari, who has been in a Karachi jail since his wife's dismissal, denies any involvement in Murtaza's killing.
